title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the 1966 'cristaux' file around the letter to Tate. It is the technical start of a contravariant Dieudonné theory D(G)=Hom(G,W) for unipotent group schemes over an arbitrary base S=Spec A of characteristic p. The neighbouring pages show this: Cor. 3 gives Ext^1(H,W)=0 for W=lim_n W_n (colimit along V); Prop. 4 shows that Hom(G,W_n) is smooth for G killed by V^n over a possibly non-perfect field; §5 introduces D(G) with its F, V and Witt-vector structure.

Lemma 1. Let S=Spec A with A of characteristic p, and work with fppf sheaf Ext. Then Ext^1(G_a,G_a) is the free A-module on the classes F^i e (i≥0). Equivalently it is the free left A[F]-module on e, where e is the class of W_2 viewed as an extension of G_a by G_a. Concretely, extensions are symmetric polynomial 2-cocycles, because G_a-torsors over an affine scheme are trivial. Modulo coboundaries these are spanned by a·Φ^{p^i}, where Φ(x,y)=(x^p+y^p-(x+y)^p)/p is the Witt cocycle, and pushforward by F equals pullback by F. Grothendieck reduces 'by limit' to A=F_p and cites Demazure–Gabriel. The reduction really works by base change: the cocycle complex is defined over F_p and is split there.

Lemma 2. Let H⊂G_a be a subgroup scheme such that, locally on S, G_a/H ≅ G_a via an additive polynomial f, so H=Ker f; α_p is the basic example. Then:
- o) R^{n-1}_*: Ext^1(H,W_n)→Ext^1(H,W_1) is bijective.
- a1) V_*: Ext^1(H,W_{n-1})→Ext^1(H,W_n) is zero; equivalently the connecting map Hom(H,G_a)→Ext^1(H,W_{n-1}) is surjective. This uses the sequence 0→W_{n-1}→W_n→G_a→0.
- a2) A further transition map Ext^1(H,W_1)→Ext^1(H,W_{·}) is zero.
- b) Restriction Ext^1(G_a,W_n)→Ext^1(H,W_n) is surjective; equivalently Ext^1(H,W_n)→Ext^2(G_a/H,W_n) is zero.
- c) Ext^1(G_a,W_n) is a right A[F]-module generated by the class of W_{n+1}, i.e. 0→W_n→W_{n+1}→G_a→0.

Proof for n=1: o) is trivial. b) follows from the local vanishing Ext^2(G_a/H,G_a)=0, which comes from Ext^2(G_a,G_a)=0 locally. c) is Lemma 1. Reference given: DG V §1 2.2. General n: by induction on n.

Purpose: a1) makes the transition maps in lim Ext^1(H,W_n) zero, which yields Ext^1(H,W)=0 (Cor. 3). By dévissage into α_p's this gives exactness of Hom(-,W) and smoothness of Hom(G,W_n) on the next page. That is the basis of D(G)=Hom(G,W) over non-perfect bases.
errors: In c) the module structure is marked 'à droite', i.e. via pullback by endomorphisms of G_a. For n=1 this does not agree with Lemma 1, which is 'à gauche'. Pulling back by multiplication by a gives e∘a = a^p e, so the right A[F]-span of e consists only of A^p-combinations of Φ^{p^i}. If A is not perfect, t·Φ with t∉A^p is not in this span. As literally stated, 'c) n'est autre que le lemme 1' therefore holds only over perfect A. For non-perfect A one needs the left action as well; for n≥2 that left action is by W_n(A).

a2) as transcribed (Ext^1(H,W_1)→Ext^1(H,W_{n-1}) zero) cannot hold for n=2, where the map is the identity: Ext^1(α_p,G_a)≠0, e.g. the restriction of W_2. Probably the intended map goes into W_n via V^{n-1}, or a2) is meant only for n≥3 inside the induction.
'Par limite on peut supposer A=F_p' is really a flat base-change argument, since the cocycle complex is defined over F_p and splits there; this is harmless.
The general-n induction is only sketched ('par récurrence sur n'), and the hypothesis on H is written ambiguously.

ideas.what: Ext^1(G_a,G_a) over an arbitrary F_p-algebra A is the free left A[F]-module on the Witt extension W_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lazard; Demazure–Gabriel; Oort (Commutative group schemes, LNM 15, 1966)
ideas.where_published: Demazure–Gabriel, Groupes algébriques (over fields); Oort LNM 15

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1966 sets up Ext-vanishing for H⊂G_a with Witt sheaves over an arbitrary characteristic-p affine base, as input for D(G)=Hom(G,W) over non-perfect bases (cf. next page). The individual lemmas are standard over perfect fields. The relative version is a modest, mostly routine extension, already implicit in later work.
missed.quote: Soit H un sous-schéma en de G_a, tel que loc. on ... G/H est loc. isom à G_a ... b) Ext^1(G_a,W_n)→Ext^1(H,W_n) surjective
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents an early unpublished attempt at relative unipotent Dieudonné theory via Hom(-,W) in the crystals period. Historically interesting, but not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard Witt-group Ext computations, essentially Demazure–Gabriel ch. V, extended to an arbitrary characteristic-p base. The interest is historical: they are groundwork for D(G)=Hom(G,W) over non-perfect bases in 1966. There is a small left/right inconsistency in c).
transcription_corrections: Lemma 1 begins 'Soit S=Spec(A) de car. p' (the struck-out word is a mis-start of Spec); this page is not 'k parfait' as in the previous page's transcription.
The hypothesis on H probably reads 'tel que loc. on ait H = Ker f, où G_a/H est loc. isomorphe à G_a (opération f ...)' rather than 'H ≃ G_a'.
In o) the map is R^{n-1}_*: Ext^1(H,W_n)→Ext^1(H,W_1) (restriction/projection W_n→W_1), as transcribed.
The Demazure–Gabriel reference is written 'II §3 4.6'; the later marginal reference 'V §1 2.2' attaches to the n=1 proof.
